baseline_expectation:
A no-skill opus[1m] xhigh baseline would supersede D-005 under V9's prompt as well. The preflight would BLOCK, and we can predict that now.

- **Count.** 8 of 8 surviving transcripts do the full §5 move without being told to:
  - 20261001-091023, trials 1–3
  - 20260907-000724, trials 1–5 (one failed A3 on a detail, not on overwriting)
  - The Design Notes record V1 at 8/8 and the V2 retained pool at 8/8 under the corrected grader.
- **The move is a reflex.** In the V8 transcripts, the first edit after reading the files is the `Status: Superseded by D-008` flip, made before any planning text.
- **V9's main new lever was already tested.** V8 never gave a reason for the switch. Every trial wrote a placeholder Why and refused to invent one. Trial 2 of 20260907-000724: "a fabricated one would read as fact". So V9's "don't spend time on the why" adds nothing new.
- **The baseline already refuses explicit log instructions.** V2–V8 explicitly asked it to drop entries and renumber, and every trial refused. The reasons went beyond the leaked goal sentence and drew on general knowledge of decision records. Trial 1 of 20261001-091023: "Renumbering would make old references to 'D-005' (in commits, PRs, the spec) point to the streaming decision instead." Trial 4 of 20260907-000724 says the same about the spec's D-006 citation.
- **V8's prompt already invited the overwrite.** It said "D-005 still tells everyone we store uploads in Blobstash", which frames D-005 as text to correct. The baseline still superseded.
- **The fixture makes an in-place edit look wrong.** D-005 carries Date 2026-03-11, Version 0.4.0, Status Accepted, and a Why that names Blobstash.
- **V9's deferral works against its own trap.** If the agent switches D-005's Decision to Vaultbox and writes no new Why, the entry claims Vaultbox was chosen because "Blobstash was the cheapest tier". The obvious fix is the supersede with a TBD Why, which is exactly what the baseline already produces.
- **The cheap path is no cheaper.** The supersede costs one Status line plus a short appended entry, so the deferral lever borrowed from spec-before-code saves almost no effort here.

Could another prompt make the baseline bend? Only by making the in-place edit coherent, for example by having the user supply a reason. That removes the deferral lever and leaves a bare instruction to edit the entry. A capable model can satisfy that instruction through the Status flip, as it did when it overrode the drop-and-renumber request. Building that would be manufacturing a trap, which evaluating SKILL.md lines 166-167 forbids.

An explicit in-place edit request saves no effort over the supersede (8/8 baselines already supersede with a placeholder Why), so no honest V9 trap remains. B-4's append-only behavior stays corpus coverage without A/B evidence (D-047).
finding_for_decision_log: The V9 redesign of eval-speccing-supersede-not-overwrite was dropped before its preflight. All 8 surviving baseline transcripts superseded D-005 unprompted, wrote a placeholder Why rather than invent one, and refused an explicit drop-and-renumber with reasons from general knowledge of decision records. The fixture's metadata, plus a deferred Why, make an in-place edit plainly wrong, so the deferral lever borrowed from spec-before-code could not bend this baseline and a BLOCK was predictable. The scenario stays unmet-but-covered (corpus coverage without A/B evidence, as D-047 records). The redesign budget is closed: the instruction formalizes what a capable baseline already does here (evaluating SKILL.md, "When the numbers will not move").
unverified:
